title: Formula versus circuit noise thresholds
formal: Put \(\beta=(3-\sqrt{7})/4\). For \(0\le p<1/2\), let \(\mathcal C_p(n)\) be the finite noisy circuits defined below. Define reliable computation at noise \(p\) by \[\operatorname{Reliable}(p)\iff \exists\delta\in(0,1/2]\ \forall n\ge1\ \forall f:\{0,1\}^{n}\to\{0,1\}\ \exists C\in\mathcal C_p(n)\ \forall x\in\{0,1\}^{n}:\Pr[C(x)=f(x)]\ge1/2+\delta.\] Is the following proposition true? \[\forall p\in[0,1/2):\quad \operatorname{Reliable}(p)\iff p<\beta.\] In particular, the proposition includes impossibility at \(p=\beta\).
definitions:
A circuit is a finite directed acyclic graph with labeled input sources \(x_1,\ldots,x_n\), noiseless constant sources \(0,1\), and one designated output wire. A computational gate has one or two ordered input wires and an arbitrary fixed Boolean truth table on those bits. Wires may connect a source or an earlier gate to any number of later gates; both inputs of a gate may come from the same predecessor. There are no other gates, external coins, auxiliary inputs, or oracle operations. A gate-free output is allowed to read one source directly.

For every computational gate \(v\), independently sample \(Z_v\in\{0,1\}\) with \(\Pr[Z_v=1]=p\). Evaluate the DAG in topological order. If the gate truth table applied to its received bits gives \(b\), its actual value is \(b\mathbin{\oplus}Z_v\), where \(\oplus\) denotes addition modulo two. Every outgoing wire carries this same actual value. All gate failures are mutually independent and independent of the input; wire values sharing a predecessor need not be independent. Input sources and wires are perfect. All computational gates, including NOT and any output gate, have exactly the same flip probability \(p\); no noiseless output decoder is supplied.

The probability in the target is only over this finite product of gate-failure distributions, for a fixed input \(x\). The circuit and its wiring and truth tables may depend on the real parameter \(p\), the integer \(n\), and the entire function \(f\), but not on the actual input \(x\) or realized failures. The advantage \(\delta\) may depend on \(p\), but is chosen before \(n\) and \(f\). Circuit size, depth and construction time are unrestricted, and no uniform algorithm constructing the circuits is required. A formula is the special case where every computational gate has at most one outgoing wire; an input variable can still occur on multiple leaves.
answer_criterion: Give a complete mathematically correct proof checked in Lean of the displayed universal equivalence or its logical negation, in the specified independent gate-flip model. The same positive advantage must work for every input length and every Boolean function at each fixed noise level. The boundary \(p=\beta\) is part of the claim. A theorem only for formulas, only for a restricted gate basis, or with a separate noiseless decoder does not decide this circuit proposition. A negative resolution of reliable computation must rule out all finite circuit sizes; failure of one construction is insufficient.
why: The problem asks how much unreliable local computation can be tolerated when arbitrary redundancy and reuse are available. It would determine whether sharing intermediate noisy values changes the fundamental threshold already known for formulas.

importance.reason: A sharp reliability boundary for general classical computation, separating the effects of gate errors from circuit size and design effort.

context_blocks.text: The task concerns whether arbitrary computation remains possible at all under local errors, even when unlimited redundancy is permitted. The target keeps a positive correctness margin independent of the function and its number of inputs. It is not a circuit-size overhead problem or an average over randomly chosen inputs.

Unger’s theorem gives the sharp formula boundary \(\beta=(3-\sqrt{7})/4\), including failure of universal reliable computation at equality, and explicitly conjectures the extension to circuits. Formulas cannot reuse an intermediate noisy gate value; circuits can, so independent gate failures do not make the received signals independent. The positive formula result below \(\beta\) also provides circuits.

The later formulation of reliable computation in Definition 2.1 of Shutty, Wootters and Hayden uses one advantage for all Boolean functions, as here. Their survey distinguishes the symmetric two-input formula threshold from the known general-circuit upper bound \(1/2-1/(2\sqrt{2})\). Their main asymmetric model permits gate-dependent errors, including noiseless XOR, and its proposed circuit extension is conditional. Those statements do not settle the identical-noise circuit claim.

The July 2025 essay revisits established circuit-noise bounds and discusses majority gates of higher arity. Its stated scope does not supply the missing exact threshold for arbitrary two-input circuits.

progress.text: The two-input formula threshold, including its boundary, is established; the unrestricted circuit counterpart is stated as a conjecture.
The revised asymmetric-noise paper retains distinct formula and circuit bounds and makes its circuit strengthening conditional.
A later expository manuscript revisits noise bounds and higher-arity majority gates; its abstract and opening model were checked for scope.

category_assignment.reason: The main target is the computational power of noisy Boolean circuits, rather than a channel coding rate.

sentences: Each gate of a Boolean circuit independently flips its computed output with the same probability.
The circuit may reuse noisy intermediate values and may be arbitrarily large.
The question asks whether universal reliable computation is possible exactly below the known two-input formula threshold.
Reliability requires one positive correctness advantage that works for every Boolean function and input length at the chosen noise level.
A resolution would determine whether sharing intermediate computations changes the fundamental tolerance to gate errors.
